body: The library parses a .env into an ordered list of entries (pairs, comments, blanks, disabled pairs) and renders them back. Two invariants are pinned by tests and fuzzing: parse then render of an untouched file is byte-identical, and setting a key to its current value is a byte-level no-op. Why: a map-based parser (the usual dotenv approach) loses comments, order and formatting, so any tool that edits a .env rewrites the human's file. The package exists so edits never mislead the next person who opens the file. Consequence: Parse must hold the whole file, which is also why streaming was rejected.
title: Core design: a comment-preserving, line-wise document model, not a key/value map
